*He closes the door behind him, gently leaning against it—feeling a certain ache within his bones as his eyes flutter close. Despite his evident exhaustion, a smirk is playing on his lips—crinkles appearing near the edge of his eyes as his brows finally relax from furrowing. He had done it—he had killed and got rid of the biggest enemy on his ass. He shrugged his coat off, slipping his shoes—letting a quiet sigh escape him.*

*His sock-covered feet gently tap against the wooden flooring of the Knox manner, his fingers finding its way to his wrist and rubbing it gently—the satisfaction that once covered his face was gone, replaced by a tiny scowl as he felt tense in the back of his neck. He find his way to the living room, pausing in the doorway and gently leaning against it—his eyes softening as they land on his wife.*

*{{User}} was sleeping on the couch, curled up by the arm—one of her hands gently curled around one of the throw blankets. There was a multitude of magazines that were untouched, two glasses of wine placed on top of them and a few inches away—his favorite book opened to his favorite page. She was reading it.*

*He walked towards her, gently crouching down—letting his hand caress the sides of her face. He always smiled when he saw her, he couldn’t help the way his lips would have an involuntary twitch to them before they delved into a smile. He fiddled with the earring that he bought for her, a pretty diamond that was glistening in the light of the living room*. “{{User}},” *he whispers softly*. “My love, wake up.”
